title: refactor(core): one withoutDeniedFields export for the field-read rule, called by seven of the eight copies (objectui#10594)
body:
Part of #10594

Clause-②: yes

> **Seat note (`domain:ui` seat #1, first line rewritten by the seat):** `Part of`, not a closing keyword. Seven of the eight sites call the export here. The eighth, `RecordPickerDialog`'s copy, is held on a permission-boundary fork (the empty object name) that went to the decision box in objectui#10594 comment `5858046810`. It lands in a follow-up after the ruling.

## What

`@object-ui/core` exports `withoutDeniedFields(record, policy, objectName, extraKeep?)`, the field-read rule for one record, as ruled on the card (ruling comment 5852005636, letter A). The policy is structural (`isLoaded`, `checkField`), so core gains no dependency and every caller already depends on core (`fields`, `react`, `app-shell`, `plugin-detail` each list `@object-ui/core`; core lists only `@object-ui/types`).

Seven of the eight hand-written definitions are deleted or rewritten to call it. **The eighth, `RecordPickerDialog`'s copy, is held**: it behaves differently on one input, and the dispatch said to report such a fork rather than pick a side. See "Held" below.

## Census on this branch's base `13220af93`

`git grep -n -E "function (withoutDeniedFields|readableRow|fieldReadGate)" HEAD -- 'packages/*/src/**' ':!**/__tests__/**'` returns 8 definitions in **6** files. The ruling read "5 files" and the claim read "7 files"; both counted the same 8 lines. A second reading that does not depend on the names, `git grep -n "withheld = true"` over the same non-test sources, returns 6 lines in the same 6 files. There is one per row-filter body. The other two definitions are a wrapper and a predicate factory.

| # | site | shape | in this PR |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | `RecordDetailView.tsx` `withoutDeniedFields` | row filter, keeps `id` / `_id` | deleted |
| 2 | `RecordDetailView.tsx` `readableRow` | identity cache over 1, keyed on the served row (AGENTS.md rule 10) | kept; calls core |
| 3 | `fields/src/index.tsx` `withoutDeniedFields` | row filter | deleted; the lookup cell and the user cell call core |
| 4 | `LookupField.tsx` `fieldReadGate` | predicate factory, same keep set plus `idField` | deleted |
| 5 | `LookupField.tsx` `withoutDeniedFields(record, readable)` | applies 4 to a row | deleted; `recordToOption` and the search chip's avatar call core with `[idField]` |
| 6 | `RecordPickerDialog.tsx` `withoutDeniedFields` | row filter plus `idField`, **no object-name guard** | **held, unchanged** |
| 7 | `plugin-detail/src/withoutDeniedFields.ts` | row filter; module export, never a package export | module deleted; `DetailView` and `record:details` import core |
| 8 | `useRecordSearch.ts` `readableRow` | row filter, policy optional | deleted; calls core |

## Why no drawn output changes at the seven sites

- **Pass-through guard.** Core's guard is `!policy?.isLoaded || !objectName || !record || typeof record !== 'object'`, the same as sites 1, 7 and 8. Sites 3 and 4 wrote `policy.isLoaded` without the optional chain. That differs only for a nullish policy. Their types forbid one, and `usePermissions()` never returns one: with no provider it returns a frozen object whose `isLoaded` is false.
- **Keep set.** Sites 1, 3, 7 and 8 keep `id` and `_id`, which is core with no fourth argument. Sites 4 and 5 also keep `idField`, which is core with `[idField]`. The kept keys short-circuit before `checkField` in both, so the same keys are asked.
- **Identity.** The same object comes back when nothing is withheld. `readableRow`'s cache and the `row === record` test in it depend on that, and it is unchanged.
- **The chip avatar.** It used to ask the predicate about its two keys. Now it filters the option row and reads the same two keys. A key is present in the filtered row exactly when the predicate kept it. `checkField` is now asked about the option's other keys too. Both providers' `checkField` are pure lookups, so this has no effect.
- **`recordToOption`.** Its last parameter was the predicate. It now takes the policy and the object judged. It is module-private and every caller is in the same file.

## Held: the `RecordPickerDialog` copy (site 6)

Its guard is `!perms.isLoaded || !record || typeof record !== 'object'`. There is no `!objectName` test. With `objectName === ''` and a loaded policy it asks `checkField('', key, 'read')` for every key, where every other copy and the export pass the row through. For an authenticated `MePermissionsProvider`, an unknown object answers false, so it would strip the row.

Reachability, measured on the base:
- Every in-repo producer passes a non-empty name. `LookupField` renders the dialog under `referenceTo &&`, `AccessExplainPanel` under `objectName.trim() &&`, and `AssignedUsersSection` passes `'sys_user'`.
- The call runs only for the display column. The same file's `readableColumns` gate drops that column whenever `checkField('', displayField)` is false, unless the display field is the id field.

Converting it is a three-line change: import from core, call `withoutDeniedFields(toPredicateRecord(record, fieldsMeta), perms, objectName, [idField])`, and delete the local copy. The question and a recommendation are in the dev report on the card. Until it is decided, this file keeps its copy and its docblock.

## `plugin-detail`'s module

The claim asked to keep `plugin-detail/src/withoutDeniedFields.ts` as a re-export if in-flight work imports it. The in-flight branch it named, `claude/issue-10657-masked-first-paint` at `e742e22d2`, has zero occurrences of `withoutDeniedFields` in its diff against its merge base. The module is therefore deleted rather than kept as a re-export. It was never in the package entry.

## Verification (all at `bda451605`)

- **Build.** `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/app-shell^... --concurrency=2` built 28 of 28 tasks. This covers core, fields, react and plugin-detail. The core build's `check-dist-completeness` reported `1 package(s) complete (210 emitted files verified)`. `dist/utils/without-denied-fields.d.ts` declares the export.
- **Type-check.** `pnpm --filter` over core, fields, react, plugin-detail and app-shell with `run type-check` echoed all five `type-check$ tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` lines and ended `Done`, exit 0. The new pin is in core's test program: `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists it.
- **Tests.** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/core/ packages/fields/ packages/react/ packages/plugin-detail/ packages/app-shell/` was run from the repo root. Result: `Test Files 1534 passed | 3 skipped (1537)`, `Tests 18847 passed | 24 skipped (18871)`, exit 0.
- **Ablation.** One-shot, with no permanent test left behind. `ablation-replace` replaced `policy.checkField(objectName, key, 'read')` with `true` in the core module: anchor 1 to 0, blob `a0c1f59` to `554a860`. It ran the core pin plus the eleven caller FLS pin files. Result: `Test Files 11 failed | 1 passed (12)`, `Tests 52 failed | 42 passed (94)`. The one file that stayed green is `RecordPickerDialog.displayFls-10373`, the held copy, and it serves as the control. The restore was proven: blob equal to HEAD (`a0c1f59`), `git diff HEAD` empty, `git status` clean. The caller pins resolve `@object-ui/core` to `packages/core/src` through the root vitest alias, so no dist rebuild sat between the mutation and the run.
- **Narrowed lint.** `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` ran over the 9 added or modified `.ts`/`.tsx` files: 9 results, 0 ignored, 0 errors. Warnings per file equal the base version of the same file linted through `--stdin`. The config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), and no custom rule under `eslint-rules/` reads other files. So this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. The full `pnpm lint` is left to CI.
- **Gates, exit 0.** `check-control-bytes`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations` (0 new), `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:phantom-deps`, `check:esm-specifiers` (specifier leg), `check:test-path-roots` and `check:self-import`.
- **`check-changeset-claims`** (report-only). It named 7 pending changesets that mention touched files. They were read, and none describes the field-read rule.
- **`check-readme-exports --list`.** The new core README import judged `real`. Exit 2, because other packages were unbuilt locally. NOT MEASURED tree-wide; the README Export Check workflow builds every package.
- **Not run.** `check:published-dist` and `check:node-esm-load`: their workflows are path-filtered to their own scripts. The new module has no imports.

## Acceptance notes

- `fields/src/index.tsx` and `LookupField.tsx` each keep a local `FieldReadPolicy` type alias, a `Pick` of `usePermissions()`. That is a type, not a copy of the rule.
- `RecordPickerDialog`'s docblock still says `LookupField` keeps its own copy and that the helper is not public. After this PR both statements are false (LookupField calls core, and the helper is a public `@object-ui/core` export). The file is held unchanged pending the decision in objectui#10594, and the follow-up that resolves it corrects that docblock.

Changeset: `@object-ui/core` minor; `@object-ui/fields`, `@object-ui/react`, `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/plugin-detail` patch.
